repeats form of bass entry; decorated tonic pedal in bass 76-80

episodes.material: bass repeats end of subject and beginning of "countersubject"; upper voices use subject opening in two-part imitation; led to strong perfect cadence at bar 22, overlapping subject entry of bar 21
29-33 middle uses bass figures of ep.1, soprano variant of subject beginning; 33-39 figures of bars 3 and 5 combined with interchange every bar
bass repeats final figure of the answer; upper voices leaping figure alternately rising and falling
55-60 repeat of rising sequence of ep.1; 60-68 varied; upper voices allude to suspension of bar 19 toward interrupted cadence at bar 68

cadences.key: ii (diagram slash at bar 25; key line ii-vi)

countersubjects.first: bar 5 (quasi-countersubject, recognizable from rising scale of bar 7)
countersubjects.notes: "countersubject" recurs below answers at 25 and 51 but parallel fourths in bar 8 would become fifths if inverted; drastically modified above (39-41) so regarded as free part; "generally classified as one without a countersubject, though it can be regarded as being of a hybrid type"

subject.ends: seems to last until the first note of bar 5 (implied cadence)
subject.notes: first three notes decorate the dominant by lower diatonic mordent (a tone); answer starts on tonic decorated by a semitone mordent; p.6: dominant is first and third note, both answered by tonic (as in I.21), whole tone g-f-g answered by semitone c-b-c, second note treated as diatonic auxiliary; listed under special cases of tonal answers (p.10)

claims.claim: Subject entry at bar 21 implies one key melodically and another harmonically.
Final section has three subject entries, none completed in original form.
Tonic and dominant pedals frequent in second half in every voice; decorated tonic pedal 76-80.
Hybrid: generally classified as without countersubject.
